spec_match.rationale: This feature has no web-facing API at all, and the pages are built around establishing that rigorously rather than asserting it: five plausible surfaces probed with a positive and a negative control, and five real reporting mechanisms shown to point the other way. The index states the band the warning occupies — softer than the interstitial, Enhanced protection only — from the ChromeStatus entry.

interactive.rationale: A live absence prober with controls; a working seven-check markup auditor that runs over pasted markup, a deliberately bad sample, or this page itself; and a link builder that constructs the real Search Console, Safe Browsing status and review URLs from a domain you type.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index says plainly that there is no API, that the site is not told and cannot opt out, and that what a developer can do is understand the signals — which is the only honest framing available for a browser-side safety feature.

edge_cases.rationale: A malformed domain rejected by hostname shape rather than by URL parsing, which accepts nonsense; markup parsed without executing it; and the boundary table that lists the questions this tool cannot answer alongside the ones it can, with three of the five landing on 'no'.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5427561449521152 on the index and all three concept pages, with Safe Browsing, the transparency report, Search Console's security issues documentation and the social engineering policy.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: no plausible surface exposes a verdict; the absence-checking technique works; the real reporting mechanisms exist and point outward; DOMParser builds a document without executing scripts, which is what makes the auditor safe to use on hostile markup; new URL accepts nonsense hostnames; and a relative URL inherits the page's scheme. The last two are the two bugs this build shipped and fixed.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 25 assertions. Measured: all five candidate APIs absent with both controls behaving; all five confusable mechanisms present; the bad sample tripping all seven checks with eight findings while clean markup trips none; a malformed domain refused; and five links built and rebuilt correctly for three different domains, all carrying rel=noopener.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the absence counts and control state, the audit's match and finding counts, and the built link count.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px control minimums, and the wide tables in their own scroll containers.

accessibility.rationale: Every control is labelled; results are announced through aria-live; findings are counts and text rather than colour alone; the built links are real anchors with descriptive text, their purpose and their full URL, so the destination is knowable before following it — which matters more than usual on a page about deceptive links.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Fact and button rows wrap; the textarea is width:100%; the link cards are a single-column grid with overflow-wrap on the URLs; every table scrolls in its own container.

openQuestions.title: The seven checks are informed guesses, not the signals
openQuestions.detail: Nobody outside Google knows what the model looks at, and the page says so twice. What the checks encode is the shape of the published policies plus patterns that are independently defects. That is defensible and it is also the ceiling: this tool will never be able to say whether a site is at risk, only whether it is doing things worth not doing.

openQuestions.title: The audit cannot see what a page loads
openQuestions.detail: Two of the categories on the third page — a compromised dependency and a third-party ad — are the commonest causes of a finding, and a markup auditor sees neither: the injected script arrives at runtime and the ad arrives in a frame. Auditing the loaded DOM rather than the source markup would catch the first; nothing a page can do catches the second.

guidanceConsulted.query: safely parse untrusted markup without executing it
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use DOMParser to build an inert document rather than assigning to innerHTML, so scripts do not run and subresources are not fetched.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The auditor parses with DOMParser and never inserts the markup into the live document, which is asserted in the conformance suite — a tool for inspecting suspicious markup that executed it would be worse than no tool.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Conformance assertion: a script tag in parsed markup does not set a global.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible link list where the destination matters
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give links descriptive text and make the destination discoverable rather than hidden behind a label.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each built link shows its title, what it is for, and its full URL as text, and carries target=_blank with rel=noopener. On a page about links that lie about where they go, showing the URL is the minimum.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive asserts every built link has target=_blank and a rel containing noopener.

guidanceConsulted.query: validate a domain typed by a user
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Validate the shape of what was typed rather than relying on a parser that is lenient by design.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The links page now checks the hostname against a domain pattern after parsing, because new URL('https://!!!not a domain!!!') succeeds and produces a percent-encoded hostname — which it did, and which built five nonsense links before it was fixed.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive types a malformed domain and asserts the page refuses it.

summary: Three concepts for a feature with no API, where the work is proving an absence properly and then being useful anyway. The auditor found two bugs in itself: a lenient URL parser that accepted nonsense as a hostname, and an insecure-subresource check that flagged three findings against this very page because a development server on plain http makes every relative path resolve to http.
